predictions.title: UniV3 AMO swaps rely on manipulable pool spot price and caller-supplied slippage
predictions.description: The AMO executes exactInputSingle against a configured Uniswap V3 pool using caller-provided amountOutMinimum and sqrtPriceLimitX96, without validating the execution price against a TWAP or independent oracle. A permissionless attacker can temporarily move the pool price immediately before an authorized AMO transaction, causing the AMO to trade at an adverse manipulated price when the supplied minimum is permissive.
predictions.impact: The protocol's liquidity assets can be exchanged for materially less value than their fair market value, transferring value to the attacker and potentially causing treasury loss or depletion of AMO-held assets.
predictions.mitigation: Derive and enforce execution bounds from an independent oracle or sufficiently long Uniswap V3 TWAP, reject materially stale or divergent pool prices, use tightly calculated slippage limits rather than caller-selected permissive values, and consider private transaction submission for large swaps.

predictions.title: UniV2 AMO swaps can execute against attacker-manipulated pair spot prices
predictions.description: UniV2LiquidityAmo integrates directly with a Uniswap V2 pair/router and enforces only a minimum output, with no loaded evidence of an independent oracle, TWAP, or reserve-integrity check. An attacker can trade against the pool immediately before a predictable AMO swap to distort reserves and cause the authorized swap to execute at an unfavorable price, provided the configured minimum output remains permissive.
predictions.impact: The AMO can lose treasury or liquidity-manager assets through unfavorable execution, and an attacker can extract the difference as arbitrage or sandwich profit.
predictions.mitigation: Derive an execution price bound from an independent trusted oracle or sufficiently long TWAP, enforce both minimum-output and maximum-input constraints against that bound, use short deadlines and transaction-private submission where possible, and reject trades when pool liquidity or reserve movement exceeds configured limits.
